challenge: Crop occurrence, scaled assemblage percentages, divine role lists, finished beads and legendary policy accounts represent different observations. challenge: Synthetic corpora are homophonic consonant encodings of running text; real inscriptions may be formulaic, logographic or nonlinguistic. Three runs per cell.
outcome: True homophonic keys exceed their within-stratum rearrangements by 27.4, 33.2, 37.1 and 72.5 standard deviations; the published key on the real corpus by 1.2-2.4. Annealing under the correct model recovered 37-83% of tokens in seven runs and 7% in one. Language identification by half-split transfer depends on seeds: Stage 5 identified Old Tamil and Sumerian but not Sanskrit or Latin; the near-duplicate rerun identified Latin and Old Tamil, tied Sanskrit with Latin and missed Sumerian. No wrong-language model exceeded z 3.1 on novel half-B texts, while the real corpus transfers at 6.3-7.0 under all four models. Indus half B reuses 37.4% of half-A trigrams against 8.2-10.1% for synthetic corpora.

question: Do recorded cord-cluster gaps restrict published account partitions when quantities are withheld?
remedy: Explicit reference-controlled scope, quantity-free input, supplied-count and count-free rules, equal-size baseline, exact all-tie candidate sets and independent source-interval/certificate checks.
retry_when: Prospectively selected accounts where gap and equal-size rules disagree, measured uncertainty or finer attachment positions supply new evidence.
title: Do recorded cord-cluster gaps restrict published account partitions when quantities are withheld?

challenge: Repeated correct carry relations and two corrupted memberships can give a wrong positive increasing vector seven votes against six for truth. Early wrong unique answers occur before later rejection or recovery.
outcome: Across 300 fresh seeds per five conditions, the three-quarter gate recovers 281 two-swap worlds, accepts four wrong vectors and keeps fifteen ambiguities; two missing memberships give 285 correct, one wrong and fourteen ambiguous. The half gate recovers 200 four-swap worlds and accepts sixteen wrong. All final wrong vectors fail fresh relation and count checks. Twelve thousand prefixes and 384,768 subset states independently checked.
question: Can exact positive maximum consensus recover positional values after incorrect child memberships?
remedy: Retain every positive family and discrete tie, continue all prefixes, preserve incorrect accepted vectors and check withheld relations and counts. Save the exact wrong-majority witness and original development diagnostic failure.
retry_when: An independently observed collection-wide conservation relation, calibrated feature error model or source group with acquired membership/count observations supplies a new test.
title: Can exact positive maximum consensus recover positional values after incorrect child memberships?

challenge: The whole inventory must be independently available and complete; redundant fresh relations can preserve a wrong numerical ray. A static checker initially misclassified a local comprehension variable as hidden-key access.
outcome: Two hundred fresh base seeds generate 1,400 worlds and 11,200 prefixes. Under four swaps and 50% local support, complete-pool conservation changes correct/wrong/ambiguous outcomes from 133/9/58 to 190/1/9. Misdeclared completeness gives fifteen wrong accepted points. One wrong baseline passes eight rank-one fresh relations but fails independent counts.
question: Can an independently observed pooled inventory resolve numerical values when local account membership is unreliable?
remedy: Freeze observation availability, impose the collective relation without adding a support vote, retain inequalities and both scale views, independently verify all subset states and residuals, and preserve the checker repair beside unchanged inference hashes.
retry_when: New physical inventory observations, measured acquisition costs or independently ranked validation rows change the available constraints.
title: Can an independently observed pooled inventory resolve numerical values when local account membership is unreliable?

challenge: One unanchored count fits every wrong ray by changing scale; account checks can repeat the same rank-one relation. Acquisition costs and measurement error are unavailable in this fixed generated population.
outcome: On KHI-04's reused 200 four-swap worlds, greedy rank rejects nine wrong rays with two checks and a counted unit anchor, or three checks without scale. Count-first needs one anchored count or two unanchored counts. Three account-first checks leave one wrong ray. Filtering collective ambiguous sets gives 199 correct absolute points and one rejected world under the stated policies.
question: Can a fixed small validation budget distinguish wrong numerical rays by independent coefficient rank or measured counts?
remedy: Freeze a post-outcome equal-check-count comparison, seal selector rows before opening targets, retain points/rays/positive families and compute exact random-subset expectations. Independently audit 33,600 deterministic records, 59,856 random-family intersections and compatible wrong witnesses.
retry_when: Fresh prospectively selected objects supply measured check costs, uncertain counts or incomplete validation membership.
title: Can a fixed small validation budget distinguish wrong numerical rays by independent coefficient rank or measured counts?

challenge: Pooling both line orders biased the control. Interior lines were counted twice, boustrophedon faces were misread, and segmenter agreement was omitted.
outcome: Complete lines recur elsewhere more often than windows crossing the division: 23 faces against 4, with 42 ties, under the conservative line order (p = 0.0003). Results survive shifted-division, deduplication and numeral-line controls in review. The Dirichlet-process segmenter places a boundary at 76 of 76 divisions against 37% of other positions. Indus alternation (0.029) lies inside every matched comparison range and is descriptive.
question: Do catalogued line divisions fall at recurring-unit boundaries, and do segmented Indus units show Kober-style stem alternation beyond readable comparison corpora?
remedy: Conservative order added in v2; v3 counts lines once and excludes boustrophedon faces; segmenter agreement computed in review.
retry_when: More boundary evidence from multi-line tablets or photograph-measured spacing permits supervised segmentation.
theme: catalogued line divisions, unsupervised segmentation and alternation
title: Do catalogued line divisions fall at recurring-unit boundaries, and do segmented Indus units show Kober-style stem alternation beyond readable comparison corpora?

challenge: Dark halftone pictures cannot certify L193's earlier angular interpretation; unpictured members and unlabelled insets limit coverage. Selected count zones expose different fractions of surfaces.
outcome: L206 is the sole resolved G01 contact and contradicts a sole angular board-edge prediction. Four G02 visible-zone ranges are 2-4, 3-5, 3-5 and 2-3; their intersection is three. Coverage differs and complete-object totals are unavailable. Two source-informed model readings and all 21 targets are retained.
question: Can available labelled Lothal views resolve contact geometry and count variation within repeated-string groups?
remedy: Crop named views without pixel alterations, preserve first and second readings separately, leave topology unresolved where appropriate, avoid duplicate-view counts, compute interval intersection with scope recorded and retain missing objects in the denominator.
retry_when: Complete calibrated marked surfaces, a second resolved G01 contact junction, same-die adjudication or independent quantity observations add information absent from the current plates.
theme: Lothal repeated-string contacts and cut zones
title: Can available labelled Lothal views resolve contact geometry and count variation within repeated-string groups?

challenge: The export writes registrations and catalogue numbers run together, lists duplicate catalogue numbers in one string and writes Marshall's areas under other prefixes. A first development run misread the Lipi SEAL:C code (circular) as a cylinder and misparsed block-and-house strings, which made 18 rows ambiguous and 386 findspot comparisons disagree. A loose variant key matched copper tablets. Eleven exact-key candidates were contradicted on material or size. The census's binarized Marshall scan dropped letter strokes, OCR misplaced row numbers on both tables, and the CISI 2 scan hides its page under a faint layer.
outcome: The repository is held at commit 5c14a01; LICENSE-DATA gives the transcribed tables CC BY 4.0 and LICENSE gives the code MIT. Against the print, 0 of 30 sampled Mackay rows and 3 of 30 Marshall rows were wrong (size, serial, type); 11 further differences were found in the join sample and in rows read beside sampled rows, 7 of them Marshall serials. Of 1,269 rows, 1,146 joined (1,108 exact, 38 confirmed) to 1,134 Mohenjo-daro objects, 1,122 of them seals (85.1% of the export's 1,318 Mohenjo-daro seals); 2 rows are ambiguous and 121 unmatched with reasons. A random sample of 30 joins checked against the print and the CISI basic-data excavation numbers had 29 correct, 0 wrong and 1 unresolved (Wilson 95% 83.3-99.4%; exact joins 20 of 20). Because the export's metadata for these objects already derives from the same tables, coverage of size, material, findspot and level rises only slightly (Mohenjo-daro: both face dimensions +12, material +5, spatial unit +10, level +2), but 1,134 objects gain a field number separated from the catalogue number and a publication reference, 1,091 a size traced to the print in inches and 1,101 a level with its datum. The table and the export disagree for 27 objects on field number, 15 on size, 14 on type, 5 on material, 5 on findspot, 3 on level and 3 on thickness.
question: What do the epachayan/indus-script transcriptions of Mackay's 1938 and Marshall's 1931 seal tables contain and under what terms, how accurately do they follow the print, which rows correspond to which CISI numbers and Lipi objects, and what size, material, findspot, level and field number does each joined object gain?
remedy: Three protocol amendments, recorded before the final run and the join sample: Marshall area aliases and multi-number registration parsing; defined variant keys with the loose form dropped; adjudication of contradicted candidates against the print, with decisions in a tracked file. The type comparator and block parser were corrected to the protocol's wording. Rows were located with a Theil-Sen fit through OCR-read row numbers; Marshall rows were read on a second scan through the Internet Archive IIIF service; CISI 2 pages were rendered rather than extracted. Each regeneration of the run was checked to leave the row dispositions unchanged by hash.
retry_when: Mackay's vol. II plates or CISI 3.1 are acquired (to check Mackay No. 181 and joins above M-1659), the CISI basic data are transcribed (Q-1005, Q-1006) and can replace the registration key with a published concordance, or the epachayan tables are revised. Rerun join_tables.py into a new dated directory; do not overwrite run-2026-10-13.
theme: Acquisition, print check and join of the Mackay 1938 and Marshall 1931 seal tables to Lipi object families and CISI numbers
title: What do the epachayan/indus-script transcriptions of Mackay's 1938 and Marshall's 1931 seal tables contain and under what terms, how accurately do they follow the print, which rows correspond to which CISI numbers and Lipi objects, and what size, material, findspot, level and field number does each joined object gain?

challenge: A stronger conventional comparator had to retain the existing query identities, grouping, folds and training-only selection.
outcome: Markov top-one 34.5861%, PMB 33.8120%, PM 16.9934% on the same 8,009 masks. PMB minus Markov top-one interval includes zero; Markov top-five and bucket log loss improve. This is the conceptual Markov family with unigram-prior smoothing, distinct from the published modified Kneser–Ney estimator.
question: How does a conventional first-order Markov model compare on the exact earlier known-slot queries?
remedy: Exact correspondence checks, nested smoothing selection, paired component intervals and independent recalculation of every query prediction.

title: How does a conventional first-order Markov model compare on the exact earlier known-slot queries?

challenge: Deleting an inference factor and refitting without end events have different effects. Training transformations can incidentally recreate held-out texts.
outcome: Removing only the end factor lowers final-slot top-one from 53.95% to 48.25%. Interior-only training shuffles average 24.52% overall versus 34.59% full Markov; all-slot shuffles average 14.88%. Unigram start replacement lowers initial top-one while improving initial bucket loss. Rare-target calibration remains poor despite low overall calibration error.
question: Which learned boundaries and interior transitions support restoration?
remedy: Separate interventions, fixed original groups and smoothing, twenty saved training orders per control, logged accidental text coincidences and independent prediction checks.
retry_when: A training-only start-shrinkage or historical transition estimator changes the comparison; retain all existing mechanism endpoints.
title: Which learned boundaries and interior transitions support restoration?

challenge: Full-record floating-point likelihoods reordered two lower-ranked candidates in one query despite matching target outcomes and losses.
outcome: Top-one-selected second order reaches 37.2706%, compared with first-order 34.5861%; paired gain 2.6845 points, interval 1.9902–3.3968. Bucket loss worsens by 0.1277 bits, interval 0.0965–0.1589. Top-five and top-ten differences are small. All 8,009 query outcomes independently checked.
question: Does second-order context improve restoration on the saved artifact-held-out masks?
remedy: Preserved the failed reviewer and original predictions. Exact rational full-record likelihoods certified the two ties in a separately saved review endpoint.
retry_when: A declared new smoothing model or independent evaluation corpus is available; retain probability loss beside exact guesses.
title: Does second-order context improve restoration on the saved artifact-held-out masks?

challenge: The preceding top-one-selected second-order model improved accuracy while worsening probability estimates.
outcome: All five folds choose backoff-only and reproduce every first-order query outcome: 34.5861% top-one and 5.11943 bits bucket loss. All 8,009 masks independently reviewed.
question: Does selecting second-order smoothing by inner probability loss retain the extra context?
remedy: Froze a separate loss-selection protocol before execution; retained model class, grid, folds and queries. Recorded reused-benchmark model-development status and both outcomes.
retry_when: New smoothing or a fresh evaluation population can test the accuracy/loss tradeoff without another adaptive comparison on the same masks.
title: Does selecting second-order smoothing by inner probability loss retain the extra context?

challenge: The extra history weight is algebraically equivalent to effective strength alpha+kappa+alpha*kappa/N, leaving equivalent grid pairs. The benchmark had already guided earlier model development.
outcome: All five outer folds select pure first-order backoff from eighteen frozen candidates. All 8,009 distributions equal M1. The closest finite candidate is .00846–.00929 inner bits worse. Independent flat counts, complete-chain probabilities, calibration and 10,000 paired component-bootstrap draws pass.
question: Can extra training-count-dependent shrinkage improve probability prediction while retaining useful second-order histories?
remedy: Freeze the equivalence, remove duplicate candidates before fitting, reuse documented masks/folds, and preserve the negative result without changing the loss objective. Verify 13,045 contexts and 3,859 exact rational identities.
retry_when: A different probability model or new independently reviewed observation block changes the test beyond this completed count-shrinkage family.
title: Can extra training-count-dependent shrinkage improve probability prediction while retaining useful second-order histories?

challenge: The British Museum served a Cloudflare challenge to scripted requests, so most of its records were read only from a saved listing; the Smithsonian API required a key; the Penn CSV lacks field numbers and bibliography; the V&A API terms forbid storing responses for more than four weeks; OCR of the CISI 1 basic-data pages missed many numbers; the CC0 Met and Cleveland seals carry no findspot or number; several joins rest on CISI 3.1 numbers that the project cannot check.
outcome: Seven institutions harvested on 13 October 2026. Inscribed Indus originals: Metropolitan 5 and Cleveland 3 (CC0 with photographs, no findspot or number), Penn 5 Chanhu-daro seals (CC BY 4.0 CSV of 430,871 rows; plus 4 uninscribed seal-amulets and 38 casts), V&A 2 inscribed originals among 4 reviewed attributed records (one modern impression and figurine head IS.9-1951 outside inscription scope), British Museum 7 with a stated inscription among 27 listed Indus stamp-seals, Art Institute of Chicago 0, Smithsonian 0 (20 casts in 539,615 bulk records). 86 museum records were decided: 27 exact or confirmed joins, 19 of them new against the census, raising the confirmed museum-join lower bound from 68 to 87. Of the census's 46 open records, 16 are confirmed, 21 ambiguous with candidate sets, 8 unmatched and 1 uninscribed. Objects with a museum accession rise from 5.84% (older export) and 6.90% (with census joins) to 7.24% (340 of 4,695). Sixteen families gain their first museum number. Six newly joined families gain an axis, including two that had no dimension before; the other four already had at least one axis. One gains a finer provenance note, and none gains an openly licensed image. Five museum objects are candidate additions to the corpus (CISI H-224; Banawali NM 3714; Dholavira DHR-22198, DHR-6032, DHR-7860). The original 26 joins were supported, 0 qualified and 0 wrong (100%, one-sided 95% lower bound 89%). The reviewer recovered Indian Museum 10377/A7252/C.2803 as family 2194 through Marshall 1931 vol. II p. 403 row 199, bringing the census-scope lower bound to 84. Recall search found hits for 10 of 59 non-joined rows, four confined to one family, with no search-derived join. See verification/independent-check.md and REVIEW-CHANGES.md.

challenge: Finite inversion can leave the simplex; a flexible corrected estimator can still lose to a prior-matched simple baseline. An unspecified boundary fallback was found, with no main case using it.

Held-out redundancy is 0.573 for full text and 0.167 for the fifteen-class skeleton; the preprint's formula gives at most 1,980 consonants (about 790-1,760 under corrections) against 473 in the 50 longest texts. 69.2% of 1,747 published readings match the key's skeleton; most departures add unwritten consonants.

challenge: Inscriptions may be formulaic names or titles rather than running speech; the model is built from Vedic and classical text. Annealed optima partly exploit the model, so they bound achievable fit rather than estimate a true key.
outcome: Order gain under an order-5 DCS model: key -0.393, 1.2 sd above 1,000 within-stratum rearrangements of its own values (89.5th percentile); 2.0-2.4 sd under unsandhied-only training or anusvara->m; an order-only statistic places it inside its rearrangements in all settings (z -0.55 to +0.60). Held-out Sanskrit spans +0.29 to +0.42; i.i.d. strings -0.435; published readings -0.442. Within-stratum optima with unchanged consonant counts reach +0.19 to +0.23; fits to scrambled texts +0.02 to +0.04 (real order -0.22 to -0.33). Unconstrained optima (+0.47 to +0.69) delete 22-46% of signs as vowels. Under matched freedom, half-split transfer z is 7.7 Sanskrit, 8.6 Latin, 8.1 Old Tamil, 6.4 Sumerian, and 6.3-7.0 on half-B texts without near-duplicates. Stage 3e failed through a rare-class artefact and is preserved.

challenge: Mohenjo-daro supplies 917 of 1,430 seals; the site breakdown is post hoc with small counts; motif codes come from catalogues and M-895 is a fragment; common names would also spread across cities.
outcome: 1,430 complete single-line seals from named South Asian sites; 65 texts recur on 174 seals, 41 at more than one site. Frozen test: same-site share of duplicate pairs 0.473 against 0.448 (p 0.31, ratio 1.06). Length-stratified null: 0.473 against 0.382 (p 0.032). Post-review breakdown: Mohenjo-daro duplicates at chance (59 against 60.2 same-site pairs), Harappa 10 against 6.0, other sites 7 against 1.5 (p 0.002); about 15% of shared texts wholly local, compatible up to 25%. Identical pairs of four or more signs exceed a bigram model 3.1- to 5.3-fold; none among 445 seals of six or more signs. Motif concordance comes from unicorn pairs (88 of 89 matches); 1 of 42 pairs with another animal matches. Of 16 sealings matching seals (6 texts), 13 (4 texts) match only seals elsewhere, including Lothal L-161 to L-170 with the four-sign text of Mohenjo-daro fragment M-895.

challenge: Published area anchors differ in extent and date; open bounds lack maxima; functional contrasts are represented by one port, craft and rural site each. Frozen area-law sign 520 q=0.044, minimum/maximum q=0.044/0.047; without the two cities q=0.387; amended-law q=0.223. No sign's area association survives the amended grouped law across 17 sites (ten have fewer than 20 readable objects). Known square motifs are 1,246/1,609 unicorn, HHI 0.605434. Unicorn versus rare clean texts average 4.794505 versus 4.019355 positions, q 0.0012; sign-distribution divergence fails exact-length conditioning, exploratory q 0.20525. Complete square-seal size n=1,027, CV 0.288599; adjusted length/area slope 1.158998 positions per doubling, q 0.0002. All five analytical outputs and the supplement reproduce; 149 checks pass, zero fail, with 108 reference tails recomputed. Post-launch amendment (Exploratory): no corrected richness outlier among eight sites, minimum q 0.177867. All-face readable top-3/top-6/top-20 shares are 18.6417/27.5143/48.7629 percent; unique-text readable shares are 18.2844/25.1666/46.4945 percent. Terminal 740 is 874/1,256 occurrences in 2,497 clean texts; expected ending objects 299.082 against 874 observed, excess 23.0243 points (95% whole-object interval 21.5005 to 24.4975); TAB:I context q 0.158466. Harappa 203 known Period-3 square motifs have raw-label heterogeneity q 0.007 and interval-time q 0.0194. The 720 dating assignments yield an at-least-95% C-minus-B change envelope of -24.8600 to +85.7669 points; the dated scope spans 700 years. Core known motifs are 1,236/1,604 unicorn; external known motifs 15/27 Gaur, including 13/13 known external circular motifs. Type-conditioned q values are 0.0094 for unicorn geography and 0.0105 for Gaur; restricted Gulf/Mesopotamia Gaur q 0.0172. New verifier: 760 passes, zero failures; original endpoints preserved. Second follow-up: the expanded 18-site area comparisons (4,452 readable objects) have minimum q 0.177/0.146/0.156/0.167 across four vectors. Period q 0.007 concerns 3C labels sharing 2200-1900 BCE; reviewer 3C-only p 0.0006. Unambiguous 3B 6/7 and 3C 112/123 do not contradict persistence. Original endpoints remain Frozen evaluation, amendments Exploratory, and arithmetic/reproduction checks Verified computation.

The post-launch lecture amendment also asks whether inventories exceed a shared sample-size curve, concentration matches the lecture, 740 is terminal, motifs persist across interval-dated Harappa phases, and Gaur dominates external finds.
remedy: Preserved a pre-outcome protocol and source table; grouped complete object payloads inside type/site blocks; corrected across specified outcomes; retained both original and dated exploratory reference laws; excluded zero/range scalar dimensions with a local audit; saved witnesses and failures locally; wrote source notes and deterministic verification without changing shared files. Added the dated protocol amendment, separate site extents, four production/iconography precedents, code mapping audit, corrected nested-label copy and archived source metadata; consolidated identical checks and documented OneDrive plotting unavailability. Current revision audit: 395 passes, zero failures; 1,670 known online-only plotting files left unopened.

outcome: A manuscript, conditional theory and 15-claim evidence map join independent delivered-output bounds, actual renewal operations, joint work windows and historically available enactment. Shared repair and learning develops a concrete alternative to separately costly training. The framework explains why urban form, residents and practical knowledge can have different persistence outcomes; a particular Harappan-to-textual contribution remains a separate historical test.
question: What minimum functional conditions does a complex society need over a stated horizon, and how can longevity and renewal traces make those conditions archaeologically testable?
remedy: Define outcome, boundary, horizon and distribution before necessity claims; include carried inventory, substitution, imports, co-production and action information. Commission independent mathematical, source and manuscript review. Preserve 12 selected starting-byte snapshots and a 16,316-file start inventory, append navigation over current bytes, and retain earlier endpoints and local-only source witnesses.
retry_when: A predeclared service sequence or common sampling frame supplies independent demand/supply bounds, dated replacement operations and participation evidence. Extend with a new dated empirical study and include short-lived, interrupted and uncertain cases.
theme: Conditional minimum functions, renewal inference and practical knowledge
title: What minimum functional conditions does a complex society need over a stated horizon, and how can longevity and renewal traces make those conditions archaeologically testable?

challenge: Purposive coverage cannot estimate field-wide omission or establish general novelty. Acquired articles and selected reading differ; book access, publisher challenge pages, edition identity and shared witnesses limit scope.
outcome: The literature frame records 28 sources, including 25 primary works read at declared scopes, 45 observations and seven prospective comparison records. Direct predecessors cover simultaneous reproduction, viable futures, repair and learning, joint scheduling, polycentric organization and coupled institutional pathways. Inspected duration/network studies do not supply the demand, initial-output, import and renewal inputs needed by the proposed archaeological inference procedure.
question: What existing theories and recommendations address the continuing provision of complex societies, and what archaeological measurements would develop them?
remedy: Preserved actual reading depth, query history, source loci, edition corrections, failed routes and local-only witnesses. Source integrity passes 312 checks and branch packaging passes 129; neither reanalyzes the published studies.
retry_when: A new close predecessor changes the bounded assessment, or a systematic sample of a defined literature tests the prevalence of a specific measurement. Do not repeat a broad priority claim from this purposive frame.
theme: Economic reproduction, maintenance, viability and archaeological persistence
title: What existing theories and recommendations address the continuing provision of complex societies, and what archaeological measurements would develop them?

challenge: Results depend on action costs, skill eligibility, shock severity, observation timing and the specified horizon. Technical selection does not establish distributed implementation, fairness, historical frequency or archaeological parameters.
outcome: A frozen 36-state model enumerates 32 worlds, finite horizons and infinite sets. Budget 1 with aging skill permits three primary safe transitions without shocks, whereas nonaging skill permits indefinite survival. Budget 2 exceeds mean work 4/3 but cannot sustain state (1,1,1) indefinitely under separate costs. A post-baseline shared repair/training law enumerates 16 worlds and removes selected deficits: budget 1/no-shock and budget 2/all original supports become indefinitely viable from the primary state. Dependency cuts and seven accounting controls qualify provider counts and additional delivery.
question: Can working services lack a feasible replacement trajectory, and how do shared deadlines, aging expertise and repair-based learning affect it under stated laws?
remedy: Independent baseline reconstruction passes 5,218 checks; six counterexamples delimit broader implications. Reviewer severity and timing variants preserve the baseline. The separately frozen shared-operation law passes 1,133 reviewer checks and 1,968 independently written coordinator checks. Actual operations are counted once, with carried inventory and enactment conditions explicit.
retry_when: Independent historical or experimental evidence supports a changed wear, timing, learning-cost, supply or participation law. Preserve these endpoints; a new invented law should name the new premise and its test rather than imply archaeological calibration.
theme: Joint renewal, skill replacement, shared operations and dependencies
title: Can working services lack a feasible replacement trajectory, and how do shared deadlines, aging expertise and repair-based learning affect it under stated laws?

challenge: Segment statistics became unreliable after the rehearsal. The numeral-order calibration failed on Ur III because of the value definition, and the typology table is unverified.
outcome: Indus initial-sign entropy exceeds final-sign entropy: asymmetry +0.260 against a shuffle range of -0.017 to 0.018, and +0.149 without the 35.2% of texts ending in 740. In comparison corpora the statistic changes sign with unit and genre: Ur III seal legends score -0.204 by sign and +0.079 by word. It is therefore descriptive, and every candidate language remains tied under the frozen rule.
question: Does a structural profile of Indus texts separate candidate language families when compared with readable seal and record corpora?
remedy: A pre-computation amendment substituted whole-text statistics. The calibration cause is reported, and the typology status is stated.
retry_when: At least two head-initial and two head-final seal-legend corpora are measured at sign and word level with the same code.
theme: whole-text structural profile and language-family typology
title: Does a structural profile of Indus texts separate candidate language families when compared with readable seal and record corpora?

challenge: A concurrent allograph study overlapped step 1. Steps 2-5 ran before step 1's endpoint. Review found overstated conclusions, a missing protocol output and several small code faults.
outcome: Diagnosis saved as a direction memo with an interactive map of 158 paths. Six steps ran under a protocol recorded before outcomes. Graphic families improve prediction of rare signs, mostly through information already in the Wells order. Harappa tablet texts pair with their images within genre, with no detectable transfer from copper to seals. Catalogued line divisions fall between recurring units. Stroke values are more tied to neighbouring signs than Ur III counts are. Unsupervised segmentation and alternation fail to discriminate at Indus scale. Indus texts close on a small sign class, a descriptive property. Every ledger description failed at least one frozen prediction, and every candidate language remains tied.
question: Which analytical mistakes have kept the project from a substantive result, and what do sign-list, image-text, segmentation, numeral, rehearsal and structural tests on material already held establish?
remedy: Step 1 was scoped to a different question. Seventeen review findings were accepted, with dated amendments, new endpoints for steps 2 and 3, rewritten reports and recorded responses. Earlier runs are preserved.
retry_when: A head-final seal-legend corpus, photograph-measured sign spacing, a within-deposit seal and sealing frame or a shuffled-order human sign coding becomes available; reuse the frozen code on the new population.
theme: diagnosis of the research program and a six-step structure-before-meaning plan
title: Which analytical mistakes have kept the project from a substantive result, and what do sign-list, image-text, segmentation, numeral, rehearsal and structural tests on material already held establish?

question: Do original catalogues and museum images support the modern marked-weight packets?
remedy: Preserve source-specific descriptions and measurements, reject HTML as a PDF, retain provisional accession joins, separate creation and deposition, and preserve the earlier fit. No new fit was run.
retry_when: Independent SB/AS concordance, conservation/weighing history, all-face marked photographs, dated assemblages or AS13855 modern registration resolves a source disagreement.
theme: Susa mass, mark and context source audit
title: Do original catalogues and museum images support the modern marked-weight packets?

challenge: The Tondur impression is dark; the modern 408 object identity and a common depth unit are missing. The compound image route returned 403 XML and the 2018 route returned 500 HTML. An extracted name and chapter end needed correction.
outcome: The original 2005 report joins a proposed 408 reading to AGM-2, depth 1.40 m, stratum 2 and drawing 2. The original Tondur account joins three reported horizontal strokes to three beds in Panchanampadi cave. Alagankulam_044 joins letters, a separate graphic and context; Alagankulam_004 supplies a registered photographed stroke specimen.
question: Can source numeral readings be joined to physical referents or registered contexts?
remedy: Acquire originals, read the tables visually, retain author hypotheses and source dates, separate neighbouring caves, preserve candidate concordances and response formats, and apply independent visual and pixel review.
retry_when: A readable Tondur impression plus bed census, original 408 accession, exact graffiti/Tamili concordance, calibrated vessel capacity or independently documented specimen quantity becomes available.
theme: South Indian original numeral and specimen contexts
title: Can source numeral readings be joined to physical referents or registered contexts?

challenge: The API supplies separate context margins without joint specimen quantities or dates. Apparent full-book downloads were a brochure and a preview. Complete component naming excluded useful compounds in the initial calculation.
outcome: Acquired the 2026 catalogue volumes and 48-route web snapshot. Counted 480 plain-stroke occurrences and 194 explicit stroke compounds; 142 have one stroke block and one other component. Found four literal cross-route identifier differences and independently confirmed missing stroke and base/variant discrepancies at 4.19C.
question: Which South Indian catalogue connections provide a finite stroke population and specimen targets for numerical tests?
remedy: Preserve string identifiers and source namespaces, inspect actual PDF page counts, keep raw inputs local-only, retain the 115-form endpoint and declare a separate 194-form membership refinement, compare printed specimen tables and preserve digital discrepancies.

title: Which South Indian catalogue connections provide a finite stroke population and specimen targets for numerical tests?

challenge: Full-register object/string closure yields a 180-text component and token-weight effective component count 123.1. Grammar classes are only partly stable; all primary folds select the largest state count. UNKNOWN events collapse distinct unseen graphics, and the class model has poor unknown-bucket calibration. Generic HMM induction already has Tiwari2026 precedent. Backoff families were designed after exposed outer outcomes.
outcome: On 1596 unique texts and 8009 tokens, the primary class grammar loses 0.472591 bits/token against tuned Markov and gains 0.291203 over position. The exploratory Markov-plus-class mixture gains 0.055708 bits/token over the equally tuned Markov-plus-position mixture, with conditional component-bootstrap interval [0.043647,0.067463]. Six synthetic controls show grammar gains under invented administrative and compositional accounts; an exact semantic twin has likelihood ratio 1. Learned class/production inventory, late-attachment hypotheses and frozen next-data predictions are retained.
question: Can the stochastic grammar recommendation be carried into learned class productions with grouped held-out prediction, and can those classes improve matched sign-level backoff?
remedy: Preserved run-v1, wrote separate post-outcome protocols and runs-v2/v3, matched mixture grids/alphabets, verified normalization/forward scores/closure and independent positional mixture arithmetic, retained source priors and synthetic identifiability witness, and froze a later-object prediction recipe.
retry_when: A source-checked genuinely excluded/new object population permits evaluation of the frozen class and position backoff recipes. Semantic scenarios require independent object-use, issuing-group or contents joins. A revised grammar/UNKNOWN calibration requires a new protocol and output, preserving current failures.
theme: Learned sign classes, conditional-length grammar prediction and compositional field hypotheses
title: Can the stochastic grammar recommendation be carried into learned class productions with grouped held-out prediction, and can those classes improve matched sign-level backoff?

challenge: Recent HMM/administrative precedents limit priority claims. Graphic sequences cannot identify semantic labels shared by equal observation laws. Post-outcome method families use exposed data. Prototype uniqueness does not induce the original copy-weighted allocation law. Recorded face completeness and independent ancient use remain unresolved.
outcome: A bounded census records 20 sources and 22 recommendations. The grammar package preserves its standalone failure and an exploratory 0.055708-bit mapped-token class increment over matched positional backoff. The carrier package finds repeated bundles and 17 descriptive companion classes with variable tall-stroke modules; role conditioning removes adjusted sign-pair maxima. A proposed standing-capacity token use cycle connects licensing and canonical allocation through issue, presentation, redemption and retention phases. An exact synthetic anchor example formalizes contextual information and copied-witness dependence.
question: Which two proposals beyond the Bonta work can be developed with new code, measured outcomes, explicit rival functions and adversarial review?
remedy: Use distinct contributors and dated outputs, preserve 690 prior-file pins, credit inspected sources, independently reconstruct probabilities and allocation tails, retain the prototype counterexample, narrow the administrative result after face-role control, and freeze new-text and context predictions. Bulk sources and reconstructible derivatives remain local-only.
retry_when: Fresh source-checked texts can test the fixed prediction recipe, or independent physical use, manufacture, content, quantity or bearer observations distinguish explicit record mechanisms. Further retuning on the exposed corpus requires a new exploratory endpoint and does not provide fresh contextual evidence.
theme: Source recommendations, parallel grammar/carrier research and proposed token use cycle
title: Which two proposals beyond the Bonta work can be developed with new code, measured outcomes, explicit rival functions and adversarial review?

challenge: Two interpretation failures in the original report; two decimal-comma mass errors, 111 false grids, seven caption leaks and missed unit attribution. Printed dimension inconsistencies remain. Small-weight heterogeneity fits fractional, absolute-error, offset and two-unit models; its physical cause remains unidentifiable. Restricted precedents and complete Gulf assemblages remain missing.
outcome: Corrected 2,058-entry catalogue (938 Greater Indus), preserving the frozen endpoint. Dholavira certain intact 5?100 g weights: n=90, unit 13.716133821 g, signal CV 1.591329596%, bootstrap unit 13.641322627?13.899021570 g. Small 1.3?5 g weights: n=147, unit 14.279643148 g, CV 5.777083713%, interval 13.973939745?14.574185919 g. The pooled 14.003 g scale blends groups. Canonical western reference 13.65 g: 125 geometric and 29 close hits among 701, versus jitter means 148.716 and 38.5375. These counts give no evidence of Indus-standard weights in western assemblages. Verified 129 likelihoods, 203 cosine points and 6,309 western scores; 20 frozen files unchanged.
question: How closely do complete catalogue weights fit declared Indus/local series, and how does fit vary by site, class, material, shape, preservation and context?
remedy: Dated post-review amendment; preserved original protocol, code, prose and all frozen outputs; repaired parser and flagged rather than imputed source inconsistencies. Refit mass bands and 75 strata, compared alternative error/fraction models and Ascalone analytical lists, used canonical western units and 2,000-draw chance controls, removed cat.220 from interpretation, corrected source metadata and independently checked arithmetic.
retry_when: Calibrated repeated reweighing with rounding resolution, wear and manufacture records, reconciled DHR identities/contexts/classes, original restricted precedent texts or complete Gulf assemblages provide new evidence. Any changed explanation or western attribution test requires a new dated protocol and endpoint.
theme: Indus and western archaeological weight metrology
title: How closely do complete catalogue weights fit declared Indus/local series, and how does fit vary by site, class, material, shape, preservation and context?
